# Conflict Sandbox — scenario authoring guide for LLMs

Conflict Sandbox (https://noahdemar.github.io/conflict-sandbox/) is a browser tool
that plays animated, narrated battle-map scenarios: units moving on real roads,
strikes with ballistic arcs and explosions, status effects, sensor views, lighting
by real sun position, and a scripted camera with captions.

A scenario is a single JSON document. To make one, produce JSON that validates
against the schema, then load it in the app (see "Loading" below).

- JSON Schema: https://noahdemar.github.io/conflict-sandbox/schema/scenario.schema.json
- Complete example: https://noahdemar.github.io/conflict-sandbox/examples/river-crossing.json

Output ONLY the JSON document when asked for a scenario — no prose, no comments,
no trailing commas.

## Top-level shape

Use the exported file wrapper (recommended):

{
  "format": "conflict-sandbox-scenario",
  "version": 1,
  "duration": 60,                // timeline length in seconds
  "roster": [ ...RosterEntry ],  // optional; gives units better silhouettes
  "scenario": { ...Scenario }
}

A bare Scenario object is also accepted.

Scenario keys: name, subtitle (place and date line for the opening title
card), sources (list of references for the closing card), factions, units, arrows, territories, labels, strikes,
keyframes (all required arrays except name), plus optional effects,
environment, duration.

## Conventions that matter

- TIME is timeline seconds from 0 to `duration`. Every event has a time
  (appearAt, destroyedAt, launchAt, start, keyframe time...). Keep all times
  within the duration.
- COORDINATE ORDER: `points` arrays are [longitude, latitude]. Units and
  labels use separate `lat` and `lng` fields. Do not swap them.
- IDS must be unique within their list; references (factionId, arrowId,
  fromUnitId, targetUnitId, unitId, targetUnitId, followUnitId, rosterId)
  must point at existing ids.
- Keep each camera shot (gap between keyframes) at least as long as its caption
  takes to read aloud: roughly 1 second per 2.5 words, plus half a second.
- Captions are read aloud by text-to-speech, so write them to be spoken:
  no dotted acronyms ("US", not "U.S."; "AM", not "a.m."), no bracketed
  asides, no abbreviations like "approx.", "e.g.", "vs.", "km" (spell them
  out), no "~", "/" or "&". Prefer plain words over symbols and write
  numbers the way you'd say them. The app normalizes common cases, but
  clean text sounds best.
- Be factual for real events and mark anything invented or approximate in the
  caption or name, e.g. "(approx.)", "Illustrative:", "Hypothetical:".

## Factions

{ "id": "f_blue", "name": "Blue", "color": "#3a6fc0", "affiliation": "friend" }

affiliation: friend | hostile | neutral | unknown. It sets military symbol frame
shape, air-defense targeting and thermal colouring (hostiles glow red).

## Units

Required: id, factionId, type, name, lat, lng, appearAt.
type: infantry | armor | artillery | air | naval | missile | hq.

The icon silhouette is picked from the unit name (and roster name), so name
things concretely: "T-72", "BMP-1", "Technical", "D-30 howitzer", "BM-21 Grad",
"HIMARS", "F-15E", "AH-64", "MQ-9 Reaper", "B-52", "AC-130J", "Chinook",
"Operator 1-1" (a single person), "K9 team", "Imaging satellite".

Optional:
- heading (degrees), arrowId (follow a route), destroyedAt, leavesAt (removed
  from the scene, e.g. boarding), rangeKm (range ring)
- sensorKm: terrain-aware line-of-sight area for ground units
- airDefenseKm: engagement envelope that turns red when enemy aircraft enter
- landAtEnd (aircraft set down at route end instead of loitering)
- altitudeKm (+ orbitRole "relay" | "imaging", captureAt): renders a satellite
  in 3D at that altitude above its ground track

Aircraft without landAtEnd circle over the end of their route. Ground vehicles
sharing one route queue, drive in column and halt in line automatically; they
pull away and brake smoothly and slow down on uphill stretches.

## Arrows (routes)

Required: id, factionId, points ([lng, lat] list), name, appearAt, duration
(seconds to traverse). A unit follows a route by `arrowId`.

- Ground units snap to real roads by default (followRoads: false to disable).
- hideLine: true = move along the path without drawing an arrow (good for
  individual people).
- times: one absolute time per point for precise pacing with holds
  (repeat a point with a later time to wait there). Overrides duration pacing.
- hideAt: stop drawing the arrow after this time.

## Strikes

Required: id, lat, lng, name, size (0.1 small arms … 1.5 large bomb), appearAt
(impact time).

The visual is chosen from `name`:
- guns: "30mm", "chain gun", "cannon", "rifle", "small arms" → tracers, sparks
- bombs: "JDAM", "GBU", "Mk 82", "bomb" → dropped, big fireball, smoke column
- shells: "howitzer", "105mm", "mortar", "fire mission" → arcing round, dirt
- anything else → missile/rocket with motor glow and smoke trail

Optional: fromUnitId + launchAt (fly from that unit; without launchAt the
flight time is derived from weapon type and distance), targetUnitId (impact
follows that unit's position at impact time — use this for moving targets),
salvo + spreadM (multiple rounds), targetStrikeId (interceptor).

Pair a destroyed unit's destroyedAt with the impact time of the strike that
hits it.

Realism: keep shooters within real weapon reach (e.g. Grad about 20 km,
122mm/155mm howitzers 15 to 30 km, GMLRS about 85 km, Hellfire about 11 km,
30mm cannon about 4 km, small arms under 1 km). Give munitions flight time
that grows with distance, and don't fire from units before they appear or
after they are destroyed. Timelines may compress time, but keep ground moves
within a couple hundred times real vehicle speed. The importer lists any
violations.

## Status effects (`effects`)

{ "id": "fx1", "kind": "radio", "unitId": "u_def", "start": 8, "duration": 4, "label": "CALLING FIRES" }

kind: radio | datalink (needs targetUnitId) | jamming (radiusM) | panic |
wounded (crippled, smoking) | noammo.

## Territories and labels

Territory: id, factionId, points ([lng, lat] ring), name, appearAt, duration
(fade-in). Optional `label` draws large faint text across it.

Label: id, text, lat, lng, size, color, appearAt. Optional `flag` (ISO country
code, e.g. "us") or `facility`: oil | gas | refinery | airbase | port | power |
base | hq | bridge | hospital | town.

## Camera, captions and sensor views (`keyframes`)

{ "id": "k1", "time": 0, "lng": 35.05, "lat": 48.45, "zoom": 12, "pitch": 0,
  "bearing": 0, "caption": "Opening line" }

- zoom: ~4 region, ~9 city, ~13 neighbourhood, ~17–19 individual buildings.
- pitch 0 = top-down; 45–65 for cinematic angles.
- followUnitId + followMode "track" keeps a unit centred; orbitSpeed rotates.
- sensor: "nvg" (night vision) or "thermal" for that shot.
- media: { src, caption, credit, anchor: [lng, lat], anchorRadiusM } shows an
  image beside a site (src must be a URL the site can load).
- Captions are narrated during playback (viewers choose voice or text only).
  narrate: false makes a line text-only.

## Environment (optional)

{ "startHour": 21.5, "endHour": 5.9, "date": "2018-02-07", "utcOffset": 3,
  "windDirDeg": 65, "windKph": 14, "haze": 0.15,
  "cloudCover": 0.3, "precipitation": "none", "precipIntensity": 0.5 }

Lighting follows the real sun for that date, time and place (night, dawn,
twilight bands at world scale). endHour may be less than startHour to cross
midnight. hourKeys: [[seconds, localHours], …] makes the clock jump (hours may
exceed 24, e.g. a cut to the next morning). Wind steers smoke, rain, snow and
dust. cloudCover (0..1) flattens the light; precipitation is none | rain |
snow | dust. Use the real weather for real events when known.

## Loading

1. In the editor: Import → paste JSON (validated with exact error messages)
   or choose a .json file.
2. By URL: https://noahdemar.github.io/conflict-sandbox/?scenario=<URL of a
   publicly readable JSON file that allows cross-origin requests>
   (e.g. a GitHub Gist "raw" link).
3. Share → copy a view or edit link to send the loaded scenario to others.

If validation fails, fix exactly the paths reported (e.g.
"/scenario/units/3/lat must be number") and resend the whole document.
